newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater figure Susan McDougal to stay in jail.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater figure Susan McDougal to stay in jail.

text.p: - A federal judge refused Monday to release Susan B. McDougal from the contempt-of-court sentence she began serving last September for refusing to cooperate with Whitewater special prosecutors.

"The Court determines that there is a realistic possibility that continued confinement might cause McDougal to change her mind and testify" before a grand jury, Judge Susan Webber Wright wrote in Little Rock.

Lawyers for President Clinton's former business partner argued that her 10 months' incarceration had demonstrated she did not intend to break her silence and there was no further legal basis for keeping her behind bars.

In the 1970s, McDougal and her then husband, James B. McDougal, were joined by Clinton, then governor of Arkansas, and his wife as investors in an Arkansas real estate project called Whitewater. The project ultimately failed, as did the savings and loan business owned by James McDougal that underwrote Whitewater.

Both McDougals were convicted in May 1996 of fraud and conspiracy in a case brought by the Whitewater prosecutor, Kenneth W. Starr, who has been trying to determine if deposits from McDougal's saving and loan, Madison Guaranty, were illegally funnelled to the Whitewater project.

James McDougal quickly agreed to cooperate with Starr's probe, but his former wife refused. Susan McDougal said she feared the prosecutors would charge her with perjury unless her answers pleased them.

Susan McDougal was sent to jail, and the contempt-of-court citation that could keep her there through next March does not count against the two-year sentence she received for her role in the Whitewater case.
McDougal said she refused to answer when Whitewater prosecutors asked her if President Clinton had testified truthfully when he appeared as a defence witness in the McDougals' trial.
Clinton said under oath that he had no knowledge of an improper $300,000 loan to Susan McDougal. Prosecutors said a portion of the loan was diverted to prop up the Whitewater project.
